headline: Business Insider reports that some early users of personal AI agents such as Instinct and Meta's Muse have deleted or restricted them after privacy scares.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a real trend with named users and company replies, but based on four users among dozens of social-media complaints.
importance_line: People weighing whether to give an AI agent access to their email and accounts face a real trade-off, but the cases are anecdotal and the companies say they protect users' data.
summary: Business Insider reports that four early adopters, among dozens raising similar concerns, said they deleted or limited the agents because of the email, account and payment access they need, citing reports of an agent reading one-time login codes without being asked and a login attempt apparently from Iran. Meta says Muse has strong privacy protections and Instinct, an invite-only agent service, says users can disconnect accounts and delete data, while The Information reports Muse has more than 3 million weekly users.
notes: Read in full. One user could not establish that Instinct's systems were compromised; the report notes this.
